newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fletcher sees Canada strike avoidable.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher sees Canada strike avoidable.

text.p: New Zealand conglomerate Fletcher Challenge Ltd said on Thursday it believed a threatened strike at the company's Canadian pulp and paper maker could be headed off and it was prepared to make some concessions.
"Yes, I believe the strike (at Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd) can be avoided," Fletcher's chief executive Hugh Fletcher told reporters after a business briefing here.

The 2,400 union workers at the company's three British Columbia pulp and paper mills voted last month in favour of a strike if necessary after talks collapsed over the company's demand for productivity and workplace improvements.

Fletcher said the traditional confrontational approach to industrial issues had to change, and British Columbia had to be seen as not only a good place in which to invest but also as a reliable supplier.
Workplace practices such as demarcation lines and stopping machines running at Christmas had to go if the operations were to be internationally competitive, he said.
However, Fletcher Challenge was prepared to make concessions when talks with unions resumed on Friday, he said.
"There are certain things which we definitely believe we must achieve if we are going to have the environment in which we can invest continuing money into those mills," he said.
"There are other things which are not black and white - is it a two percent or one percent wage increase per annum - obviously there is room in those things to reach an agreement," he said.
